title: United Kingdom: packaging producer registration, above threshold
summary: A UK-established business that supplied or imported more than 25 tonnes of packaging in the previous year AND had worldwide turnover of £1 million or more must register with the environmental regulator and report packaging data. Below both thresholds there is no pEPR registration obligation.

required_evidence.label: Proof of registration with the environmental regulator

sources.title: The Producer Responsibility Obligations (Packaging and Packaging Waste) Regulations 2024 (S.I. 2024/1332)
sources.note: Fetched the statute directly, resolving the note in the previous draft that the S.I. number was unconfirmed: it is S.I. 2024/1332. Reg. 23 defines 'large producer' and 'small producer'; reg. 24(2) sets the small-producer threshold this requirement models — more than £1,000,000 turnover in the relevant prior year AND more than 25 tonnes of packaging supplied — matching the draft's thresholds exactly. Reg. 25 is the actual registration/reporting obligation. FINDING the draft does not yet model: this requirement treats every producer past the threshold identically, but regs. 23-25 set materially different duties for 'small producer' (register + report annually) versus 'large producer' (register + report every 6 months + buy PRNs/PERNs + submit a compliance certificate + pay a disposal fee — large producer starts above 50 tonnes AND £2m turnover per reg. 24(1)/GOV.UK's own threshold table). A design partner who is a small producer would currently be told they need evidence a large producer's obligations imply, or vice versa, once this is more than a single 'proof of registration' evidence type. Tabeen decision needed: split into small-producer and large-producer rows, or explicitly scope this row to registration only (which is common to both tiers) and add the large-producer-only duties as a separate future row. Also note: S.I. 2025/1369 amends the 2024 Regulations from 1 January 2026 — none of the amendments found so far touch regs. 23-25, but re-check before the 2026 reporting cycle.
